comments.body:
## Mathematical Review

See linked 'Critic Analysis' doc for the full writeup. Summary below.

**Verdict:** The STATEMENT is TRUE (I independently confirmed multiplicativity numerically: two-copy nu_p equals [nu_p]^2 to 1e-4 for d in {2,3}, x in {0.3,0.6}, p in {1.5,2}); the single-copy closed form nu_p(Phi_x)=[(x+a)^p+(d-2)a^p]^{1/p}, a=(1-x)/(d-1), matches random pure-state maximization to <1e-2 for d in {2,3,4}). HOWEVER the submitted proof is INCOMPLETE.

**Correct & complete parts:** Lemma 1 (CPTP/unital, Kraus identity verified), Lemma 2 (pure-state reduction via Bauer max principle), Lemma 3 (single-copy spectrum {lambda_+,lambda_-,a^{(d-2)}} and the monotone-in-P maximization, uses only p>=1; c=1 degenerate case handled), Lemma 4 (lower bound), Lemma 5 (d=2 via King's unital qubit theorem, Pauli transfer matrix diag(1,2x-1,1,2x-1) correct).

**CRITICAL GAP (blocking):** Section 7 — the case d>=3, 1<=p<=2, which is the ENTIRE mathematical content for d>=3 — is asserted as 'Theorem (King-Nathanson-Ruskai)' with NO proof, only a one-paragraph sketch and an unverifiable citation (no journal/volume/year/page). The cited 'theorem' is verbatim the conclusion to be proved => circular. The crux claim 'covariance + operator convexity of t^p force a product-state maximizer' is asserted with no argument; no Lieb/trace inequality is invoked.

**Why the easy routes fail (independently verified):** For d>=3, Phi_x is NOT entanglement-breaking (Choi partial transpose min eigenvalue <= -0.4 for d in {3,4}, all x), so Holevo-Shor-King EB multiplicativity does NOT apply; and Phi_x is not a qubit channel, so King's d=2 theorem does NOT apply. The d>=3 upper bound genuinely requires the channel-specific argument that is missing.

**Secondary gap:** No reduction of the two-copy optimizer to a product state. The covariance group U(x)Ubar acts diagonally and is NOT transitive on pure states of C^d(x)C^d, so symmetry alone cannot reduce to one product test state; the proof must bound Tr[(Phi_x(x)Phi_x)(rho)]^p for entangled inputs via a half-channel/Lieb decomposition tied to 1<=p<=2, and show equality forces a product.

**To finish:** supply a full King-Nathanson-Ruskai-style proof (dual-norm + Holder + operator convexity for 1<=p<=2, or block-diagonalization over sym/antisym subspaces of C^d(x)C^d), OR give an exact published reference with theorem number, stated verbatim, all hypotheses verified, and confirm it is not a restatement of the target.

Verified the standard shortcuts are unavailable: for d>=3, Phi_x is NOT entanglement-breaking (Choi PT min eigenvalue <= -0.4, d in {3,4}, all x) => Holevo-Shor-King EB multiplicativity inapplicable; and Phi_x is not a qubit channel => King's d=2 theorem inapplicable. comments.body:
### GAP 2 (proof-gap, supporting) — no reduction of two-copy optimizer to a product state for d>=3

(Filed as a comment; create-issue route blocked for this problem id.)

To close the d>=3 upper bound one must show the optimal pure input |Psi> in C^d (x) C^d to Phi_x (x) Phi_x can be taken to be a product, OR bound ||(Phi_x(x)Phi_x)(|Psi><Psi|)||_p <= [nu_p(Phi_x)]^2 for ALL entangled |Psi>. solution.tex does neither.

Obstruction the proof ignores: the covariance group U(x)Ubar acts DIAGONALLY and is NOT transitive on pure states of C^d(x)C^d, so symmetry alone cannot reduce to a single product test state. A real proof must bound Tr[(Phi_x(x)Phi_x)(rho)]^p for entangled inputs (e.g. dual norm ||X||_p=sup_{||Y||_q<=1}|Tr(XY)| + Holder + operator convexity for 1<=p<=2, or block-diagonalization over symmetric/antisymmetric subspaces), and show equality forces a product, linking back to the single-copy spectrum of Lemma 3. All of this is absent.
